title: Do Digital Platforms Bring Micro and Small Enterprises Closer to Financial Inclusion? Evidence from a Higher-Order PLS-SEM Approach in Peru
content: This study examines whether the participation of micro and small enterprises (MSEs) in digital platforms is related to their financial inclusion in Piura, the region with the highest level of business informality in Peru. Using a quantitative, cross-sectional design, 372 MSEs were analyzed through PLS-SEM with reflective–formative higher-order constructs. Platform participation was positively and significantly related to financial inclusion (β = 0.714; p < 0.001; R² = 0.510; f² = 1.04), with medium predictive power. Digital management integration (w = 0.618) and platform commercialization (w = 0.449) defined digital participation, whereas digital accessibility did not make a significant contribution. Access and usage were significant components of financial inclusion, but the perceived quality of the conditions was not. The relationship held under two alternative data-cleaning rules (β = 0.647–0.790). The results suggest that digitalization brings MSEs closer to financial services through the information and flows it generates rather than through infrastructure, without improving the conditions of access on its own, which supports information asymmetry theory in contexts of high informality.
